name: Robert Half Inc.

profile.description: Robert Half Inc. provides specialized talent solutions (contract and permanent placement in finance & accounting, technology, and administrative roles) and business consulting through its Protiviti subsidiary [10]. Q3 2026 revenue was $1.359B (+0.4% YoY reported), with talent solutions growing 1.6% on an adjusted basis — its first growth since 2022 — while Protiviti revenue fell 2.9% to $483.5M [1][12]. CEO Keith Waddell, with the company since 1986 and CEO since December 2019, maintains a $0.59 quarterly dividend that has exceeded pre-financing cash generation year-to-date [1][5].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The business mix — contract talent, permanent placement and Protiviti consulting — is essentially unchanged over five years, though Fortune named Robert Half one of America's Most Innovative Companies in 2026 for its tech-enabled recruiting [4][10]. AI Deployment (2/2): Robert Half runs its proprietary AI Recommended Client (ARC) system in production to direct recruiters to likely-hiring clients, earning a CIO 100 award and a Stevie award for Best AI/Machine Learning Solution [6]. Market Share (1/2): Forbes ranked it No. 1 among America's Best Professional Recruiting Firms for 2026, but revenue fell from $7.24B (2022) to $5.38B (2025), so it is a leader in reputation rather than a share gainer [7][11]. Pipeline (0/2): No new service lines with launch timelines were disclosed; guidance focuses on recovery of existing segments [1]. R&D (0/1): No R&D is reported [11].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Robert Half positions itself as a global leader in talent solutions and business consulting — clear about what it does and whom it serves, but not distinctive versus staffing peers [5][10]. Community Impact (0/2): Research surfaced SBTi-validated environmental targets in the 10-K but no quantified community or charitable program [8]. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention data was found; headcount stands at ~14,500 after three years of revenue declines, and the company faces wage-and-hour class actions from recruiters alleging misclassification [9][10]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying was identified in the last 12 months; open-market buybacks have also slowed to $6.8M year-to-date [1].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on 10 dividend-sleeve metrics (weighted sum 7.79 of 12). Strengths: a debt-light balance sheet (D/E 20%), forward P/E of 22.2 (0.95), 22 consecutive years of dividends since 2004, and a 5-yr dividend CAGR of 11.7% ($1.36 in 2020 to $2.36 in 2025) [10]. Weaknesses: ROE of 9.8% (0.65), revenue growth of just 0.4% YoY (0.68) and a 5-yr revenue CAGR of 1.0% (FY2020 $5.11B to FY2025 $5.38B, computed) (0.40), a 2.3% profit margin (0.12), and a payout ratio of 193% (0.00) [10][11]. The dividend was held flat at $0.59 per quarter through 2026 after 21 straight annual increases, so consecutive years of growth is recorded as 0, and 9-month dividends of $179.8M exceeded pre-financing cash generation of $47.1M as cash fell to $321M [1].

ai_resilience.label: HIGH RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (3/9): Robert Half's own Q3 release lists AI displacement of clerical and professional roles as a standing risk, and its administrative & customer support line is still shrinking (-3.1%) while generative AI floods recruiters with homogeneous applications [1][3]. Its core franchise — placing finance, accounting and admin professionals — sits squarely in the roles AI automates, with only partial protection from tech-contract demand (+4.6% to $165.1M) and Protiviti's advisory work [1]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Waddell cites growing demand for talent to support AI transitions, but the company reports no quantified AI revenue [3].

infinite_game.summary: Robert Half has a long-tenured leadership team and once made a bold adjacency move into consulting with Protiviti, but today it is managing a cyclical and structural downturn rather than advancing a cause [5][1]. Sinek would note that it is paying out roughly $60M a quarter in dividends it no longer covers with cash generation — a commitment to shareholder optics — while revenue has fallen from $7.24B to $5.38B and AI threatens its core placements [1][11].

just_cause.analysis: The company's purpose is framed around being a global leader in talent solutions and consulting — a description of the business rather than an idealistic future state [5][10]. No evidence was found that a deeper cause drives strategic decisions (1/3).

trusting_teams.analysis: Leadership is remarkably stable — Waddell spent 33 years as CFO before becoming CEO in 2019 and has been with the firm since 1986 [5]. That continuity is offset by long-running wage-and-hour litigation from salaried recruiters alleging misclassification, so trust is adequate rather than exceptional (1/2) [9].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Public communications emphasize rankings (Forbes No. 1, Fortune Most Innovative) rather than learning from competitors, and no management commentary acknowledging rivals as benchmarks was found [4][7]. Insufficient evidence of an infinite competitive mindset (0/1).

existential_flexibility.analysis: Building Protiviti into a ~$480M-per-quarter consulting business shows the company has evolved beyond pure staffing, and it is layering AI tools like ARC onto recruiting [1][6]. But it has not reinvented its core placement model in response to AI, which is the shift its situation now demands (1/2).

courage_to_lead.analysis: Management has kept investing in proprietary AI tools and technology consulting capability through a three-year revenue decline, an example of choosing long-term capability [4][6]. Holding the dividend at $0.59 while it exceeds cash generation and buybacks fall to near zero reads more as protecting the payout than as a costly strategic bet (1/2) [1].

investment_thesis: Robert Half may be at a cyclical trough: Q3 2026 EPS of $0.49 beat the $0.47 consensus and rose 14% — the first year-over-year EPS increase since 2022 — as talent solutions returned to growth (+1.6% adjusted), permanent placement rose 5.6%, and talent-solutions gross margin expanded 0.7 points to 47.4% [1][12]. A debt-light balance sheet (D/E 20%), a 5.4% dividend yield, and Protiviti's guide to flat-to-up 4% in Q4 give operating leverage if white-collar hiring recovers [1][10].
thesis_continued: The bear case is structural: revenue fell from $7.24B in 2022 to $5.38B in 2025, the company itself flags AI displacement of clerical and professional roles, and its admin & customer support business is still contracting [1][11]. The dividend is uncovered — $179.8M paid in nine months versus $47.1M of pre-financing cash generation, a 193% payout ratio and cash down to $321M from $464M — so a dividend cut is a real risk, while profit margin is just 2.3% and Protiviti gross margin compressed sharply earlier in 2026 [1][2][10].
key_catalysts: Sustained recovery in talent solutions after the first growth since 2022 (+1.6% adjusted in Q3 2026), led by permanent placement (+5.6%) and technology contract (+4.6% to $165.1M) [1][12]
Protiviti returning to growth, with Q4 2026 revenue guided flat to up 4% after a -3.3% Q3 that beat the -4% to -8% guide [1]
Operating leverage from a debt-free balance sheet: Q3 operating income excluding trust swings rose 18.5% to $72.6M on flat revenue [1]
key_risks: AI displacement of finance, accounting and administrative roles — the core of Robert Half's contract and permanent placement franchise — which the company itself lists as a standing risk factor [1]
Dividend sustainability: nine-month dividends of $179.8M against $47.1M of pre-financing cash generation, a 193% payout ratio and the 2026 dividend held flat after 21 years of increases [1][10]
Wage-and-hour class actions alleging recruiter misclassification (Dorff, filed 2018) and unpaid interview time for 212,000+ workers (PAGA, filed 2015) [9]
